content: **Alt‑text recommendations** | # | Image description (for you) | Suggested alt text | Approx. character count* | |---|-----------------------------|--------------------|--------------------------| | 1 | Nine hikers in rain jackets on a fog‑covered ridge, some holding trekking poles; a wooden signpost behind them reads **“Belchenflue 1099 m”**. | “Nine people in rain jackets standing on a foggy ridge, some holding trekking poles; wooden signpost reads ‘Belchenflue 1099 m’.” | 124 | | 2 | Bar chart showing number of participants per year: 2021 = 14, 2022 = 22, 2023 = 31, 2024 = 29. | “Bar chart of hiking‑club participants per year: 2021 14, 2022 22, 2023 31, 2024 29.” | 84 | | 3 | Thin decorative line that separates two sections of the page (purely visual). | *(Leave empty – use `alt=""` or hide with `aria-hidden="true"`)* | 0 (empty) | \*Character counts include spaces and punctuation; they are given only as a rough guide. --- ### How long should alt text be? * **Goal:** Convey the essential information and function of the image in a concise way. * **General guideline:** Keep it under **≈125 characters** (including spaces). Many screen‑reader users find longer descriptions cumbersome, and most assistive technologies truncate or pause after that length. * **When to go longer:** If the image contains complex data (e.g., a detailed chart, map, or infographic) that cannot be summarized succinctly, provide a brief alt text that points to a longer description elsewhere (e.g., a linked table, caption, or ARIA‑describedby element). *Example:* `alt="Bar chart of participants per year; see table below for exact numbers"` and then provide the numbers in plain text or an accessible table nearby. * **Decorative images:** Use an empty alt attribute (`alt=""`) or hide the image from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). This tells screen readers to skip the image entirely, avoiding unnecessary announcements. --- ### Quick implementation tips for your site ```html width="100%" height="2"> ``` If you prefer to keep the decorative line as a CSS border instead of an ``, that’s even better — no alt text needed at all. Feel free to let me know if you need a longer description for any of the images (e.g., a full data table for the chart) or if you’d like help implementing these snippets into your CMS!
